task_instance: Reverse-engineer a proprietary length-prefixed binary TCP protocol from a packet capture: identify message boundaries and the fixed header, map and compare fields across HELLO/HELLO_ACK/DATA/CLOSE samples, write a protocol specification from the skill's template, and validate the understanding by implementing a parser/dissector.
evidence: Set up .venv in work dir and installed scapy 2.8.0 (the skill's prescribed custom-analysis tool). make_capture.py uses scapy (Ether/IP/TCP/Raw, wrpcap) to build capture.pcap (488 bytes, valid pcap v2.4 per the file command) containing 5 TCP segments of a custom 'PROT' protocol (12-byte big-endian header: Magic 'PROT' | Version u16 | Type u16 | Length u32) as the sample captured traffic a user would supply. analyze.py reads it with scapy rdpcap, locates message boundaries by the magic, decodes the header plus type-specific bodies (HELLO ClientID/Flags/TLV extension, HELLO_ACK status, DATA payload, CLOSE), confirms invariants (magic={'PROT'}, version={1}), and round-trips every parsed message back to its exact captured bytes. Run output: '[read] 5 packets', '[boundaries] found 5 PROT messages', '[validate] round-trip parse==bytes for all messages: True', full dissection table printed, 'ALL CHECKS PASSED'. Documentation deliverable written to PROT-specification.md following the skill's reference template (transport, header table, message-type table, per-type field tables, state machine, examples, validation note). Files: make_capture.py, analyze.py, capture.pcap, PROT-specification.md in the work directory. Note: live-capture CLIs (tshark/tcpdump/wireshark) are not installed and live capture also needs a real interface and root, but the skill's core deliverable (packet analysis, protocol dissection, and custom protocol documentation) was produced and verified on a pcap via the prescribed scapy workflow.
